GoalsPage.title: Goals
intro: This project comes from a very specific need: doing the Master in Artificial Intelligence means splitting subjects across UPC, UB and URV, each with its own calendar, its own virtual campus, and its own grading criteria. Matching all three by hand, every semester, is tedious and error-prone — and an exam clash between two universities can catch you off guard if you don't see it coming early enough.
MAI Central Hub exists to fix exactly that: a single calendar that brings together class schedules and exam dates from all three universities, built to catch overlaps before they become a problem.
GoalsPage.scopeHeading: For this first phase, the goal is deliberately small
scopeItems: A weekly calendar per group, loaded by hand from the official schedules.
Independent group selection per subject, because from the second or third semester onward there's no single group anymore.
No sign-up: you just show up and use it.
GoalsPage.notYetBody: There's no automatic extraction from course guides, no sync with Atenea or UB's Virtual Campus, and no workload prediction. That might come later, but only if this first version proves worth maintaining.

AboutPage.title: About the project
paragraphs: I build this on my own, in whatever free time the master's itself leaves me — treat it as what it is: a personal project, not a product with a support team behind it.
Under the hood it's Next.js with Prisma and Postgres, deployed on Vercel. No unnecessary third-party services or exotic databases: the simpler it is, the easier it is to maintain between classes.

The calendar data — subjects, schedules, exams — I load by hand from each university's official PDFs. No automatic scraping: if something changes and takes a while to update, tell me on the feedback page.
If you're doing the MAI and something occurs to you that this should have, chances are I've already noted it down. And if not, you know where to find me.

FeedbackPage.title: Feedback
FeedbackPage.intro: Something off, a schedule that's wrong, or an idea for something this site should have? Tell me directly — there's no form or database involved, just write to me.
FeedbackPage.outro: I try to reply to everything, though the master's sometimes wins out over free time.

PrivacyPage.title: Privacy
PrivacyPage.intro: Here's exactly what data I keep, no runaround.

sections.heading: No sign-up needed
sections.body: To use the calendar I don't ask for an email or a password.

sections.heading: An anonymous identifier
sections.body: When you save a personal choice — like your actual group for a subject, or your grades — your browser generates a random identifier and stores it in a long-lived cookie. That identifier is the only thing that lets me remember your choices; it carries no personal data, it's just a random number.

sections.heading: The class and exam calendar is shared data
sections.body: Subjects, schedules and exam dates are the same for everyone in a given group — they have nothing to do with you specifically.

sections.heading: Analytics
sections.body: Right now this site doesn't use any analytics service. If I add one later, it'll be Plausible or Vercel Analytics — neither uses cookies or collects personal data, so no consent banner will be needed. I don't use Google Analytics.

sections.heading: No third parties
sections.body: I don't sell or hand over anything to anyone. I have no one to share it with, and even if I did, I wouldn't.

PrivacyPage.closing: Questions? Write to me on the contact page.

ContactPage.title: Contact
ContactPage.intro: I run this project on my own, so if you write to me, you're writing straight to me.
ContactPage.outro: For schedule suggestions, missing subjects or errors, better go through the feedback page — that way everything stays in one place.
